messages:
nina: Quick one 1 - when I double-click the Redwood LocalServe.app (mac pkg installed), it boots a GUI wrapper that starts redwoodctl but ignores the saved `--profile` in the UI. localserve ends up using `default` and hits prod db :grimacing:
lee: Does the app actually accept flags? Spotlight/open -> .app doesn't forward args. How are you setting the profile in the UI?
nina: The app has a small field for profile name (UI prefs), I type `dev-local` and click Start. The logs show it's still loading `~/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json`.
jord: Can you run `ps aux | grep redwoodctl` after starting from the .app? Might be the wrapper writes a config file in /var/root or uses a LaunchAgent with a different HOME.
nina: Output: `nina    12345   0.0  0.1  2468  512 ??  S    10:02AM   0:00.12 /Applications/Redwood LocalServe.app/Contents/MacOS/Redwood LocalServe` 
lee: Try `open -a "Redwood LocalServe" --args --profile dev-local --debug` from terminal. That passes args via open. If that works it's definitely the GUI wrapper not mapping the UI value to argv.
nina: `open -a ... --args` works and localserve reads correct profile. GUI start log excerpt:
```
[2025-01-10T10:02:05Z] args: ["/Applications/Redwood LocalServe.app/Contents/MacOS/Redwood LocalServe"]
[2025-01-10T10:02:05Z] ui pref profile: "dev-local"
[2025-01-10T10:02:05Z] resolved config: /Users/nina/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json
```
nina: So UI pref is present but never applied.
mike: I think the wrapper is doing a two-step launch: main process (the .app exec) reads UI then spawns `redwoodctl` without passing `--profile` env/arg. If the child inherits a different HOME (LaunchServices sandboxing?), it'll fall back. Can someone dump the child process env? `ps eww <pid>` or use Activity Monitor -> Sample Process.
jord: Filed ticket RDW-DEVEX-1212: LocalServe macOS wrapper ignores UI profile; labels macos, cli, hotfix. Link: https://redwood.internal/issue/RDW-DEVEX-1212
devex-bot: New issue created RDW-DEVEX-1212 by jord. Priority: P2.
lee: Short term mitigation: add a small shim script in docs that creates an Automator app which invokes `open --args` or create an alias in `/usr/local/bin` and instruct users to run `open -a "Redwood LocalServe" --args --profile dev-local`. I'll add a note to Mac install troubleshooting.
mike: For root cause I'll grep the .app bundle: likely Contents/MacOS/Redwood LocalServe is an electron wrapper that writes prefs to a temp json and then launches `redwoodctl` via NSTask without mapping args. If so fix is to populate argv or set REDWOODCTL_PROFILE env before spawn.
nina: Thanks. I can test a dev build if you want. Also adding logs to the ticket, attaching a small recording of the UI start.
lee: Can confirm repro on Ventura 13.6 with pkg install. Not reproducible when installing via Homebrew (since Homebrew installs a symlinked binary you run from shell). So doc should recommend brew for power users until fix.
jord: assigning to eng-cli and eng-mac for triage. I'll add test-case: start via Finder double-click, via Spotlight, via open --args, and via CLI to ensure all codepaths respect UI prefs and `--profile` overrides.
nina: Appreciate it. Workaround is in docs and I can use `open --args` for now. :thumbsup:
lee: I'll add a simple Automator workflow to the docs repo and ping here when PR is ready.
devex-bot: Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1011 (macos/local-serve-workarounds)
nina: Cheers all. Leaving the sample logs I collected in the ticket.
